text: {"claims":[{"id":"c0","evidence":[{"sid":"P0.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P0.S1","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P1.S2","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P1.S3","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P0 requires all processes on one host due shared memory; P1 identifies the wal-index as shared-memory and says that forces readers onto one machine."},{"id":"c1","evidence":[{"sid":"P0.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P1.S4","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"Both passages state WAL does not work over a network filesystem; NFS is such a filesystem, so different-machine NFS use is excluded."},{"id":"c2","evidence":[{"sid":"P3.S0","rel":"refutes"},{"sid":"P5.S2","rel":"refutes"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"Same-host is necessary, not sufficient: P3 adds required locking-mode conditions and P5 says some VFS configurations fail without shared-memory support."},{"id":"c6","evidence":[{"sid":"P3.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P5.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P5.S4","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P3 allows no-shared-memory WAL with prior EXCLUSIVE mode; P5 says NORMAL first access creates the shared-memory wal-index and ties omission to prior EXCLUSIVE."},{"id":"c7","evidence":[{"sid":"P4.S0","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P4.S1","rel":"entails"},{"sid":"P4.S2","rel":"entails"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"P4 says the connection remains EXCLUSIVE while journal mode is WAL and cannot leave EXCLUSIVE until leaving WAL."},{"id":"c11","evidence":[{"sid":"P7.S0","rel":"refutes"},{"sid":"P6.S2","rel":"refutes"}],"check":null,"reasoning":"The no-block guarantee in P7 applies with synchronous NORMAL; P6 says FULL syncs on every commit, so a main thread can still block. Thus 'regardless' is false."}]}
